scenes.line1: Why does shape matter in TypeScript?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why TypeScript lets you assign objects with extra properties? Let's explore how structural typing works.

scenes.label: Shape
scenes.sub: TypeScript checks the actual properties, not the type's name.
scenes.say: TypeScript cares about the shape of your data, not the name of the type or interface.
If an object has at least the required properties, like x and y, it's compatible—even if it has extras.
Interfaces and type aliases with the same structure are treated as compatible. Only the shape matters.

scenes.question: Does TypeScript care about type names?
scenes.right: No, only the structure matters for compatibility.
scenes.say: Don't get caught thinking the name matters. TypeScript only checks the structure.
